name: Meniscal Tear of the Knee
definition: Traumatic or degenerative disruption of the knee meniscus. Degenerative tears are common on MRI and may be incidental; symptoms and mechanical findings require correlation.

typical: True locking can occur with displaced tear
Traumatic twisting onset in younger patients

investigations.MRI: MRI is preferred for suspected clinically important tear when diagnosis will alter treatment.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs assess OA or fracture but not meniscal tissue.

green: Rehabilitation emphasizing ROM, quadriceps/hip strength and function
amber: Arthroscopy is not routine for degenerative tears without true mechanical locking; selected displaced traumatic tears may require surgical review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu-sandhi/Snayu phenotype can be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Traumatic or degenerative disruption of the knee meniscus. Degenerative tears are common on MRI and may be incidental; symptoms and mechanical findings require correlation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
